name: Positron-Electron Project
notes: The ring and its interaction regions are on the SLAC campus; the PEP site marker is the SLAC campus point. The existing PEP-II record places PEP-II at the IR-2 hall (site:slac-pep-ii-ir2-babar).

circumference.quote: a larger storage ring for particle collisions (1.4 miles or 2.2 km in circumference, compared to SPEAR’s 234 m)

cms_energy.locator: CERN Courier, "The time projection chamber turns 25"
cms_energy.note: Centre-of-mass energy at which the PEP experiments (MAC, PEP-4 TPC) took the data in their publications; PEP could reach higher energies.
cms_energy.quote: which studied 29 GeV e+e– collisions at the PEP storage ring at SLAC

summary.plain: SLAC's second electron-positron collider, a ring 2.2 kilometres around that ran from 1980 to 1990 at about 29 GeV. Detectors including MAC, the PEP-4 time projection chamber and Mark II studied quark jets, the tau lepton and electroweak effects. Its ring was reused for PEP-II.
summary.technical: PEP e⁺e⁻ storage-ring collider at SLAC, 2.2 km circumference, injected by the SLAC linac, centre-of-mass energy about 29 GeV for the experiments recorded here; construction began June 1977, operation 1980-1990; experiments included MAC, PEP-4 (TPC) and Mark II; the ring was reused for the high-energy ring of PEP-II.
